25//
26// version 2.0.0 : Add new object oriented API. 1.x API is still provided.
27// * Add python binding.
28// * Support line primitive.
29// * Support points primitive.
30// * Support multiple search path for .mtl(v1 API).
31// * Support vertex skinning weight `vw`(as an tinyobj
32// extension). Note that this differs vertex weight([w]
33// component in `v` line)
34// * Support escaped whitespece in mtllib
35// * Add robust triangulation using Mapbox
36// earcut(TINYOBJLOADER_USE_MAPBOX_EARCUT).
37// version 1.4.0 : Modifed ParseTextureNameAndOption API
38// version 1.3.1 : Make ParseTextureNameAndOption API public
39// version 1.3.0 : Separate warning and error message(breaking API of LoadObj)
40// version 1.2.3 : Added color space extension('-colorspace') to tex opts.
41// version 1.2.2 : Parse multiple group names.
42// version 1.2.1 : Added initial support for line('l') primitive(PR #178)
43// version 1.2.0 : Hardened implementation(#175)
44// version 1.1.1 : Support smoothing groups(#162)
45// version 1.1.0 : Support parsing vertex color(#144)
46// version 1.0.8 : Fix parsing `g` tag just after `usemtl`(#138)
47// version 1.0.7 : Support multiple tex options(#126)
48// version 1.0.6 : Add TINYOBJLOADER_USE_DOUBLE option(#124)
49// version 1.0.5 : Ignore `Tr` when `d` exists in MTL(#43)
50// version 1.0.4 : Support multiple filenames for 'mtllib'(#112)
51// version 1.0.3 : Support parsing texture options(#85)
52// version 1.0.2 : Improve parsing speed by about a factor of 2 for large
53// files(#105)
54// version 1.0.1 : Fixes a shape is lost if obj ends with a 'usemtl'(#104)
55// version 1.0.0 : Change data structure. Change license from BSD to MIT.
56//

95// https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wavefront_.obj_file says ...
96//
97// -blendu on | off # set horizontal texture blending
98// (default on)
99// -blendv on | off # set vertical texture blending
100// (default on)
101// -boost real_value # boost mip-map sharpness
102// -mm base_value gain_value # modify texture map values (default
103// 0 1)
104// # base_value = brightness,
105// gain_value = contrast
106// -o u [v [w]] # Origin offset (default
107// 0 0 0)
108// -s u [v [w]] # Scale (default
109// 1 1 1)
110// -t u [v [w]] # Turbulence (default
111// 0 0 0)
112// -texres resolution # texture resolution to create
113// -clamp on | off # only render texels in the clamped
114// 0-1 range (default off)
115// # When unclamped, textures are
116// repeated across a surface,
117// # when clamped, only texels which
118// fall within the 0-1
119// # range are rendered.
120// -bm mult_value # bump multiplier (for bump maps
121// only)
122//
123// -imfchan r | g | b | m | l | z # specifies which channel of the file
124// is used to
125// # create a scalar or bump texture.
126// r:red, g:green,
127// # b:blue, m:matte, l:luminance,
128// z:z-depth..
129// # (the default for bump is 'l' and
130// for decal is 'm')
131// bump -imfchan r bumpmap.tga # says to use the red channel of
132// bumpmap.tga as the bumpmap
133//
134// For reflection maps...
135//
136// -type sphere # specifies a sphere for a "refl"
137// reflection map
138// -type cube_top | cube_bottom | # when using a cube map, the texture
139// file for each
140// cube_front | cube_back | # side of the cube is specified
141// separately
142// cube_left | cube_right
143//
144// TinyObjLoader extension.
145//
146// -colorspace SPACE # Color space of the texture. e.g.
147// 'sRGB` or 'linear'
148//
149
150#ifdef TINYOBJLOADER_USE_DOUBLE
151//#pragma message "using double"
152typedef double real_t;
153#else
154//#pragma message "using float"
155typedef float real_t;
156#endif
157
158typedef enum {
159 TEXTURE_TYPE_NONE, // default
160 TEXTURE_TYPE_SPHERE,
161 TEXTURE_TYPE_CUBE_TOP,
162 TEXTURE_TYPE_CUBE_BOTTOM,
163 TEXTURE_TYPE_CUBE_FRONT,
164 TEXTURE_TYPE_CUBE_BACK,
165 TEXTURE_TYPE_CUBE_LEFT,
166 TEXTURE_TYPE_CUBE_RIGHT
167} texture_type_t;
168
169struct texture_option_t {
170 texture_type_t type; // -type (default TEXTURE_TYPE_NONE)
171 real_t sharpness; // -boost (default 1.0?)
172 real_t brightness; // base_value in -mm option (default 0)
173 real_t contrast; // gain_value in -mm option (default 1)
174 real_t origin_offset[3]; // -o u [v [w]] (default 0 0 0)
175 real_t scale[3]; // -s u [v [w]] (default 1 1 1)
176 real_t turbulence[3]; // -t u [v [w]] (default 0 0 0)
177 int texture_resolution; // -texres resolution (No default value in the spec.
178 // We'll use -1)
179 bool clamp; // -clamp (default false)
180 char imfchan; // -imfchan (the default for bump is 'l' and for decal is 'm')
181 bool blendu; // -blendu (default on)
182 bool blendv; // -blendv (default on)
183 real_t bump_multiplier; // -bm (for bump maps only, default 1.0)
184
185 // extension
186 std::string colorspace; // Explicitly specify color space of stored texel
187 // value. Usually `sRGB` or `linear` (default empty).
188};

334template <typename Alloc = std::allocator<char>>
335struct basic_tag_t {
336 using allocator_type = Alloc;
337 using char_alloc =
338 typename std::allocator_traits<Alloc>::template rebind_alloc<char>;
339 using string_type =
340 std::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, char_alloc>;
341 using int_alloc =
342 typename std::allocator_traits<Alloc>::template rebind_alloc<int>;
343 using real_alloc =
344 typename std::allocator_traits<Alloc>::template rebind_alloc<real_t>;
345 using string_alloc =
346 typename std::allocator_traits<Alloc>::template rebind_alloc<string_type>;
347
348 string_type name;
349 std::vector<int, int_alloc> intValues;
350 std::vector<real_t, real_alloc> floatValues;
351 std::vector<string_type, string_alloc> stringValues;
352
353 basic_tag_t()
354 : name(),
355 intValues(),
356 floatValues(),
357 stringValues() {}
358
359 explicit basic_tag_t(const allocator_type &alloc)
360 : name(char_alloc(alloc)),
361 intValues(int_alloc(alloc)),
362 floatValues(real_alloc(alloc)),
363 stringValues(string_alloc(alloc)) {}
364
365 template <typename OtherAlloc>
366 basic_tag_t(const basic_tag_t<OtherAlloc> &rhs) : name(rhs.name) {
367 intValues.assign(rhs.intValues.begin(), rhs.intValues.end());
368 floatValues.assign(rhs.floatValues.begin(), rhs.floatValues.end());
369 stringValues.assign(rhs.stringValues.begin(), rhs.stringValues.end());
370 }
371
372 template <typename OtherAlloc>
373 basic_tag_t(const basic_tag_t<OtherAlloc> &rhs, const allocator_type &alloc)
374 : name(rhs.name.begin(), rhs.name.end(), char_alloc(alloc)),
375 intValues(int_alloc(alloc)),
376 floatValues(real_alloc(alloc)),
377 stringValues(string_alloc(alloc)) {
378 intValues.assign(rhs.intValues.begin(), rhs.intValues.end());
379 floatValues.assign(rhs.floatValues.begin(), rhs.floatValues.end());
380 for (size_t i = 0; i < rhs.stringValues.size(); i++) {
381 stringValues.emplace_back(rhs.stringValues[i].begin(),
382 rhs.stringValues[i].end(), char_alloc(alloc));
383 }
384 }
385
386 template <typename OtherAlloc>
387 basic_tag_t &operator=(const basic_tag_t<OtherAlloc> &rhs) {
388 name = rhs.name;
389 intValues.assign(rhs.intValues.begin(), rhs.intValues.end());
390 floatValues.assign(rhs.floatValues.begin(), rhs.floatValues.end());
391 stringValues.assign(rhs.stringValues.begin(), rhs.stringValues.end());
392 return *this;
393 }
394};
395

403template <typename Alloc = std::allocator<char>>
404struct basic_skin_weight_t {
405 using allocator_type = Alloc;
406 using joint_weight_alloc =
407 typename std::allocator_traits<Alloc>::template rebind_alloc<
408 joint_and_weight_t>;
409
410 int vertex_id; // Corresponding vertex index in `attrib_t::vertices`.
411 // Compared to `index_t`, this index must be positive and
412 // start with 0(does not allow relative indexing)
413 std::vector<joint_and_weight_t, joint_weight_alloc> weightValues;
414
415 basic_skin_weight_t() : vertex_id(0) {}
416
417 explicit basic_skin_weight_t(const allocator_type &alloc)
418 : vertex_id(0), weightValues(joint_weight_alloc(alloc)) {}
419
420 template <typename OtherAlloc>
421 basic_skin_weight_t(const basic_skin_weight_t<OtherAlloc> &rhs)
422 : vertex_id(rhs.vertex_id) {
423 weightValues.assign(rhs.weightValues.begin(), rhs.weightValues.end());
424 }
425
426 template <typename OtherAlloc>
427 basic_skin_weight_t(const basic_skin_weight_t<OtherAlloc> &rhs,
428 const allocator_type &alloc)
429 : vertex_id(rhs.vertex_id), weightValues(joint_weight_alloc(alloc)) {
430 weightValues.assign(rhs.weightValues.begin(), rhs.weightValues.end());
431 }
432
433 template <typename OtherAlloc>
434 basic_skin_weight_t &operator=(const basic_skin_weight_t<OtherAlloc> &rhs) {
435 vertex_id = rhs.vertex_id;
436 weightValues.assign(rhs.weightValues.begin(), rhs.weightValues.end());
437 return *this;
438 }
439};

484// Vertex attributes
485struct attrib_t {
486 std::vector<real_t> vertices; // 'v'(xyz)
487
488 // For backward compatibility, we store vertex weight in separate array.
489 std::vector<real_t> vertex_weights; // 'v'(w)
490 std::vector<real_t> normals; // 'vn'
491 std::vector<real_t> texcoords; // 'vt'(uv)
492
493 // For backward compatibility, we store texture coordinate 'w' in separate
494 // array.
495 std::vector<real_t> texcoord_ws; // 'vt'(w)
496 std::vector<real_t> colors; // extension: vertex colors
497
498 //
499 // TinyObj extension.
500 //
501
502 // NOTE(syoyo): array index is based on the appearance order.
503 // To get a corresponding skin weight for a specific vertex id `vid`,
504 // Need to reconstruct a look up table: `skin_weight_t::vertex_id` == `vid`
505 // (e.g. using std::map, std::unordered_map)
506 std::vector<skin_weight_t> skin_weights;
507
508 attrib_t() {}
509
510 //
511 // For pybind11
512 //
513 const std::vector<real_t> &GetVertices() const { return vertices; }
514
515 const std::vector<real_t> &GetVertexWeights() const { return vertex_weights; }
516};

518struct callback_t {
519 // W is optional and set to 1 if there is no `w` item in `v` line
520 void (*vertex_cb)(void *user_data, real_t x, real_t y, real_t z, real_t w);
521 void (*vertex_color_cb)(void *user_data, real_t x, real_t y, real_t z,
522 real_t r, real_t g, real_t b, bool has_color);
523 void (*normal_cb)(void *user_data, real_t x, real_t y, real_t z);
524
525 // y and z are optional and set to 0 if there is no `y` and/or `z` item(s) in
526 // `vt` line.
527 void (*texcoord_cb)(void *user_data, real_t x, real_t y, real_t z);
528
529 // called per 'f' line. num_indices is the number of face indices(e.g. 3 for
530 // triangle, 4 for quad)
531 // 0 will be passed for undefined index in index_t members.
532 void (*index_cb)(void *user_data, index_t *indices, int num_indices);
533 // `name` material name, `material_id` = the array index of material_t[]. -1
534 // if
535 // a material not found in .mtl
536 void (*usemtl_cb)(void *user_data, const char *name, int material_id);
537 // `materials` = parsed material data.
538 void (*mtllib_cb)(void *user_data, const material_t *materials,
539 int num_materials);
540 // There may be multiple group names
541 void (*group_cb)(void *user_data, const char **names, int num_names);
542 void (*object_cb)(void *user_data, const char *name);
543
544 callback_t()
545 : vertex_cb(NULL),
546 vertex_color_cb(NULL),
547 normal_cb(NULL),
548 texcoord_cb(NULL),
549 index_cb(NULL),
550 usemtl_cb(NULL),
551 mtllib_cb(NULL),
552 group_cb(NULL),
553 object_cb(NULL) {}
554};

766class ArenaAllocator {
767 public:
768 explicit ArenaAllocator(size_t block_size = 1024 * 1024)
769 : head_(nullptr), default_block_size_(block_size) {}
770
771 ~ArenaAllocator() { destroy(); }
772
773 ArenaAllocator(const ArenaAllocator &) = delete;
774 ArenaAllocator &operator=(const ArenaAllocator &) = delete;
775
776 ArenaAllocator(ArenaAllocator &&o) noexcept
777 : head_(o.head_), default_block_size_(o.default_block_size_) {
778 o.head_ = nullptr;
779 }
780 ArenaAllocator &operator=(ArenaAllocator &&o) noexcept {
781 if (this != &o) {
782 destroy();
783 head_ = o.head_;
784 default_block_size_ = o.default_block_size_;
785 o.head_ = nullptr;
786 }
787 return *this;
788 }
789
790 void *allocate(size_t bytes,
791 size_t alignment = sizeof(void *));
792
794 void reset();
795
796 private:
797 struct Block {
798 unsigned char *data;
799 size_t capacity;
800 size_t used;
801 Block *next;
802 };
803
804 Block *head_;
805 size_t default_block_size_;
806
807 Block *new_block(size_t min_bytes);
808 void destroy();
809};

815template <typename T>
816class arena_adapter {
817 public:
818 using value_type = T;
819 using pointer = T *;
820 using const_pointer = const T *;
821 using size_type = std::size_t;
822 using difference_type = std::ptrdiff_t;
823 using propagate_on_container_copy_assignment = std::true_type;
824 using propagate_on_container_move_assignment = std::true_type;
825 using propagate_on_container_swap = std::true_type;
826
827 explicit arena_adapter(ArenaAllocator *arena = nullptr) noexcept
828 : arena_(arena) {}
829
830 template <typename U>
831 arena_adapter(const arena_adapter<U> &other) noexcept
832 : arena_(other.arena()) {}
833
834 T *allocate(size_t n) {
835 if (n > SIZE_MAX / sizeof(T)) {
836#ifdef TINYOBJLOADER_ENABLE_EXCEPTION
837 throw std::bad_alloc();
838#else
839 return nullptr;
840#endif
841 }
842 if (arena_) {
843 return static_cast<T *>(arena_->allocate(n * sizeof(T), alignof(T)));
844 }
845#ifdef TINYOBJLOADER_ENABLE_EXCEPTION
846 return static_cast<T *>(::operator new(n * sizeof(T)));
847#else
848 return static_cast<T *>(::operator new(n * sizeof(T), std::nothrow));
849#endif
850 }
851
852 void deallocate(T *p, size_t) noexcept {
853 if (!arena_) {
854 ::operator delete(p);
855 return;
856 }
857 // Arena deallocation is a no-op; memory freed in bulk via reset().
858 }
859
860 ArenaAllocator *arena() const noexcept { return arena_; }
861
862 template <typename U>
863 bool operator==(const arena_adapter<U> &o) const noexcept {
864 return arena_ == o.arena();
865 }
866 template <typename U>
867 bool operator!=(const arena_adapter<U> &o) const noexcept {
868 return arena_ != o.arena();
869 }
870
871 template <typename U>
872 struct rebind {
873 using other = arena_adapter<U>;
874 };
875
876 private:
877 ArenaAllocator *arena_;
878};

1017// ---- TypedArray-based zero-copy API for maximum efficiency ----
1018
1023template <typename T>
1024class TypedArray {
1025 static_assert(std::is_trivially_copyable<T>::value,
1026 "TypedArray<T> requires T to be trivially copyable "
1027 "(uses memset for initialization).");
1028
1029 public:
1030 TypedArray() : data_(nullptr), size_(0) {}
1031
1032 T *data() { return data_; }
1033 const T *data() const { return data_; }
1034 size_t size() const { return size_; }
1035 bool empty() const { return size_ == 0; }
1036
1037 T &operator[](size_t i) { return data_[i]; }
1038 const T &operator[](size_t i) const { return data_[i]; }
1039
1040 T *begin() { return data_; }
1041 T *end() { return data_ + size_; }
1042 const T *begin() const { return data_; }
1043 const T *end() const { return data_ + size_; }
1044
1049 bool allocate(ArenaAllocator &arena, size_t count) {
1050 if (count == 0) {
1051 data_ = nullptr;
1052 size_ = 0;
1053 return true;
1054 }
1055 // Guard against size_t overflow in count * sizeof(T).
1056 if (count > SIZE_MAX / sizeof(T)) {
1057#ifdef TINYOBJLOADER_ENABLE_EXCEPTION
1058 throw std::bad_alloc();
1059#else
1060 data_ = nullptr;
1061 size_ = 0;
1062 return false;
1063#endif
1064 }
1065 void *p = arena.allocate(count * sizeof(T), alignof(T));
1066 if (!p) {
1067 data_ = nullptr;
1068 size_ = 0;
1069 return false;
1070 }
1071 data_ = static_cast<T *>(p);
1072 size_ = count;
1073 std::memset(data_, 0, count * sizeof(T));
1074 return true;
1075 }
1076
1079 void set(T *ptr, size_t count) {
1080 data_ = ptr;
1081 size_ = count;
1082 }
1083
1085 void truncate(size_t new_size) {
1086 if (new_size < size_) size_ = new_size;
1087 }
1088
1089 void clear() {
1090 data_ = nullptr;
1091 size_ = 0;
1092 }
1093
1094 private:
1095 T *data_;
1096 size_t size_;
1097};

1142struct OptResult {

1144 OptAttrib attrib;

1146 std::vector<material_t> materials;
1147 bool valid;
1148
1149 OptResult() : arena(4 * 1024 * 1024), valid(false) {}
1150
1151 OptResult(OptResult &&o) noexcept
1152 : arena(std::move(o.arena)),
1153 attrib(o.attrib),
1154 shapes(std::move(o.shapes)),
1155 materials(std::move(o.materials)),
1156 valid(o.valid) {
1157 o.attrib = OptAttrib(); // clear dangling pointers
1158 o.valid = false;
1159 }
1160
1161 OptResult &operator=(OptResult &&o) noexcept {
1162 if (this != &o) {
1163 arena = std::move(o.arena);
1164 attrib = o.attrib;
1165 shapes = std::move(o.shapes);
1166 materials = std::move(o.materials);
1167 valid = o.valid;
1168 o.attrib = OptAttrib();
1169 o.valid = false;
1170 }
1171 return *this;
1172 }
1173
1174 OptResult(const OptResult &) = delete;
1175 OptResult &operator=(const OptResult &) = delete;
1176};

1260#ifdef _WIN32
1261// Converts a UTF-8 encoded string to a UTF-16 wide string for use with
1262// Windows file APIs that support Unicode paths (including paths longer than
1263// MAX_PATH when combined with the extended-length path prefix).
1264static std::wstring UTF8ToWchar(const std::string &str) {
1265 if (str.empty()) return std::wstring();
1266 int size_needed =
1267 MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, str.c_str(),
1268 static_cast<int>(str.size()), NULL, 0);
1269 if (size_needed == 0) return std::wstring();
1270 std::wstring wstr(static_cast<size_t>(size_needed), L'\0');
1271 int result =
1272 MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, str.c_str(),
1273 static_cast<int>(str.size()), &wstr[0], size_needed);
1274 if (result == 0) return std::wstring();
1275 return wstr;
1276}
1277
1278// Prepends the Windows extended-length path prefix ("\\?\") to an absolute
1279// path when the path length meets or exceeds MAX_PATH (260 characters).
1280// This allows Windows APIs to handle paths up to 32767 characters long.
1281// UNC paths (starting with "\\") are converted to "\\?\UNC\" form.
1282static std::wstring LongPathW(const std::wstring &wpath) {
1283 const std::wstring kLongPathPrefix = L"\\\\?\\";
1284 const std::wstring kUNCPrefix = L"\\\\";
1285 const std::wstring kLongUNCPathPrefix = L"\\\\?\\UNC\\";
1286
1287 // Already has the extended-length prefix; return as-is.
1288 if (wpath.size() >= kLongPathPrefix.size() &&
1289 wpath.substr(0, kLongPathPrefix.size()) == kLongPathPrefix) {
1290 return wpath;
1291 }
1292
1293 // Only add the prefix when the path is long enough to require it.
1294 if (wpath.size() < MAX_PATH) {
1295 return wpath;
1296 }
1297
1298 // Normalize forward slashes to backslashes: the extended-length "\\?\"
1299 // prefix requires backslash separators only.
1300 std::wstring normalized = wpath;
1301 for (std::wstring::size_type i = 0; i < normalized.size(); ++i) {
1302 if (normalized[i] == L'/') normalized[i] = L'\\';
1303 }
1304
1305 // UNC path: "\\server\share\..." -> "\\?\UNC\server\share\..."
1306 if (normalized.size() >= kUNCPrefix.size() &&
1307 normalized.substr(0, kUNCPrefix.size()) == kUNCPrefix) {
1308 return kLongUNCPathPrefix + normalized.substr(kUNCPrefix.size());
1309 }
1310
1311 // Absolute path with drive letter: "C:\..." -> "\\?\C:\..."
1312 if (normalized.size() >= 2 && normalized[1] == L':') {
1313 return kLongPathPrefix + normalized;
1314 }
1315
1316 return normalized;
1317}
1318#endif // _WIN32

1352// --- integral_constant, true_type, false_type ---
1353template <typename T, T V>
1354struct integral_constant {
1355 static const T value = V;
1356 typedef T value_type;
1357 typedef integral_constant type;
1358 operator value_type() const { return value; }
1359};
1360typedef integral_constant<bool, true> true_type;
1361typedef integral_constant<bool, false> false_type;
1362
1363// --- is_same ---
1364template <typename T, typename U> struct is_same : false_type {};
1365template <typename T> struct is_same<T, T> : true_type {};
1366
1367// --- enable_if ---
1368template <bool B, typename T = void> struct enable_if {};
1369template <typename T> struct enable_if<true, T> { typedef T type; };
1370
1371// --- conditional ---
1372template <bool B, typename T, typename F> struct conditional { typedef T type; };
1373template <typename T, typename F> struct conditional<false, T, F> { typedef F type; };
1374
1375// --- is_integral ---
1376template <typename T> struct is_integral : false_type {};
1377template <> struct is_integral<bool> : true_type {};
1378template <> struct is_integral<char> : true_type {};
1379template <> struct is_integral<signed char> : true_type {};
1380template <> struct is_integral<unsigned char> : true_type {};
1381template <> struct is_integral<short> : true_type {};
1382template <> struct is_integral<unsigned short> : true_type {};
1383template <> struct is_integral<int> : true_type {};
1384template <> struct is_integral<unsigned int> : true_type {};
1385template <> struct is_integral<long> : true_type {};
1386template <> struct is_integral<unsigned long> : true_type {};
1387template <> struct is_integral<long long> : true_type {};
1388template <> struct is_integral<unsigned long long> : true_type {};
1389template <> struct is_integral<wchar_t> : true_type {};
1390template <> struct is_integral<char16_t> : true_type {};
1391template <> struct is_integral<char32_t> : true_type {};
1392
1393// --- is_signed ---
1394template <typename T> struct is_signed : integral_constant<bool, T(-1) < T(0)> {};
1395
1396// --- underlying_type (uses compiler builtin) ---
1397template <typename T> struct underlying_type {
1398 typedef __underlying_type(T) type;
1399};
1400
1401// --- ff_errc (replaces std::errc, our own enum - no system_error needed) ---
1402enum class ff_errc { ok = 0, invalid_argument = 22, result_out_of_range = 34 };
1403
1404// --- min_val (replaces std::min, avoids Windows min/max macro conflicts) ---
1405template <typename T>
1406inline T min_val(T a, T b) { return (b < a) ? b : a; }
1407
1408// --- copy_n ---
1409template <typename InputIt, typename Size, typename OutputIt>
1410inline OutputIt copy_n(InputIt first, Size count, OutputIt result) {
1411 for (Size i = 0; i < count; ++i) *result++ = *first++;
1412 return result;
1413}
1414
1415// --- copy_backward ---
1416template <typename BidirIt1, typename BidirIt2>
1417inline BidirIt2 copy_backward(BidirIt1 first, BidirIt1 last, BidirIt2 d_last) {
1418 while (first != last) *(--d_last) = *(--last);
1419 return d_last;
1420}
1421
1422// --- fill ---
1423template <typename ForwardIt, typename T>
1424inline void fill(ForwardIt first, ForwardIt last, const T &value) {
1425 for (; first != last; ++first) *first = value;
1426}
1427
1428// --- distance ---
1429template <typename It>
1430inline typename conditional<true, long long, It>::type
1431distance(It first, It last) {
1432 return last - first;
1433}

1622enum class chars_format : uint64_t {
1623 scientific = 1 << 0,
1624 fixed = 1 << 2,
1625 hex = 1 << 3,
1626 no_infnan = 1 << 4,
1627 // RFC 8259: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8259#section-6
1628 json = uint64_t(detail::basic_json_fmt) | fixed | scientific | no_infnan,
1629 // Extension of RFC 8259 where, e.g., "inf" and "nan" are allowed.
1630 json_or_infnan = uint64_t(detail::basic_json_fmt) | fixed | scientific,
1631 fortran = uint64_t(detail::basic_fortran_fmt) | fixed | scientific,
1632 general = fixed | scientific,
1633 allow_leading_plus = 1 << 7,
1634 skip_white_space = 1 << 8,
1635};

1843// Compares two ASCII strings in a case insensitive manner.
1844template <typename UC>
1845inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 bool
1846fastfloat_strncasecmp(UC const *actual_mixedcase, UC const *expected_lowercase,
1847 size_t length) {
1848 for (size_t i = 0; i < length; ++i) {
1849 UC const actual = actual_mixedcase[i];
1850 if ((actual < 256 ? actual | 32 : actual) != expected_lowercase[i]) {
1851 return false;
1852 }
1853 }
1854 return true;
1855}

1873 FASTFLOAT_DEBUG_ASSERT(index < length);

1887/* Helper C++14 constexpr generic implementation of leading_zeroes */
1888fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 int
1889leading_zeroes_generic(uint64_t input_num, int last_bit = 0) {
1890 if (input_num & uint64_t(0xffffffff00000000)) {
1891 input_num >>= 32;
1892 last_bit |= 32;
1893 }
1894 if (input_num & uint64_t(0xffff0000)) {
1895 input_num >>= 16;
1896 last_bit |= 16;
1897 }
1898 if (input_num & uint64_t(0xff00)) {
1899 input_num >>= 8;
1900 last_bit |= 8;
1901 }
1902 if (input_num & uint64_t(0xf0)) {
1903 input_num >>= 4;
1904 last_bit |= 4;
1905 }
1906 if (input_num & uint64_t(0xc)) {
1907 input_num >>= 2;
1908 last_bit |= 2;
1909 }
1910 if (input_num & uint64_t(0x2)) { /* input_num >>= 1; */
1911 last_bit |= 1;
1912 }
1913 return 63 - last_bit;
1914}
1915
1916/* result might be undefined when input_num is zero */
1917fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 int
1918leading_zeroes(uint64_t input_num) {
1919 assert(input_num > 0);
1920 if (cpp20_and_in_constexpr()) {
1921 return leading_zeroes_generic(input_num);
1922 }
1923#ifdef FASTFLOAT_VISUAL_STUDIO
1924#if defined(_M_X64) || defined(_M_ARM64)
1925 unsigned long leading_zero = 0;
1926 // Search the mask data from most significant bit (MSB)
1927 // to least significant bit (LSB) for a set bit (1).
1928 _BitScanReverse64(&leading_zero, input_num);
1929 return (int)(63 - leading_zero);
1930#else
1931 return leading_zeroes_generic(input_num);
1932#endif
1933#else
1934 return __builtin_clzll(input_num);
1935#endif
1936}

1938// slow emulation routine for 32-bit
1939fastfloat_really_inline constexpr uint64_t emulu(uint32_t x, uint32_t y) {
1940 return x * (uint64_t)y;
1941}
1942
1943fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 uint64_t
1944umul128_generic(uint64_t ab, uint64_t cd, uint64_t *hi) {
1945 uint64_t ad = emulu((uint32_t)(ab >> 32), (uint32_t)cd);
1946 uint64_t bd = emulu((uint32_t)ab, (uint32_t)cd);
1947 uint64_t adbc = ad + emulu((uint32_t)ab, (uint32_t)(cd >> 32));
1948 uint64_t adbc_carry = (uint64_t)(adbc < ad);
1949 uint64_t lo = bd + (adbc << 32);
1950 *hi = emulu((uint32_t)(ab >> 32), (uint32_t)(cd >> 32)) + (adbc >> 32) +
1951 (adbc_carry << 32) + (uint64_t)(lo < bd);
1952 return lo;
1953}
1954
1955#ifdef FASTFLOAT_32BIT
1956
1957// slow emulation routine for 32-bit
1958#if !defined(__MINGW64__)
1959fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 uint64_t _umul128(uint64_t ab,
1960 uint64_t cd,
1961 uint64_t *hi) {
1962 return umul128_generic(ab, cd, hi);
1963}
1964#endif // !__MINGW64__
1965
1966#endif // FASTFLOAT_32BIT
1967
1968// compute 64-bit a*b
1969fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 value128
1970full_multiplication(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) {
1971 if (cpp20_and_in_constexpr()) {
1972 value128 answer;
1973 answer.low = umul128_generic(a, b, &answer.high);
1974 return answer;
1975 }
1976 value128 answer;
1977#if defined(_M_ARM64) && !defined(__MINGW32__)
1978 // ARM64 has native support for 64-bit multiplications, no need to emulate
1979 // But MinGW on ARM64 doesn't have native support for 64-bit multiplications
1980 answer.high = __umulh(a, b);
1981 answer.low = a * b;
1982#elif defined(FASTFLOAT_32BIT) || \
1983 (defined(_WIN64) && !defined(__clang__) && !defined(_M_ARM64))
1984 answer.low = _umul128(a, b, &answer.high); // _umul128 not available on ARM64
1985#elif defined(FASTFLOAT_64BIT) && defined(__SIZEOF_INT128__)
1986 __uint128_t r = ((__uint128_t)a) * b;
1987 answer.low = uint64_t(r);
1988 answer.high = uint64_t(r >> 64);
1989#else
1990 answer.low = umul128_generic(a, b, &answer.high);
1991#endif
1992 return answer;
1993}

1995struct adjusted_mantissa {
1996 uint64_t mantissa{0};
1997 int32_t power2{0}; // a negative value indicates an invalid result
1998 adjusted_mantissa() = default;
1999
2000 constexpr bool operator==(adjusted_mantissa const &o) const {
2001 return mantissa == o.mantissa && power2 == o.power2;
2002 }
2003
2004 constexpr bool operator!=(adjusted_mantissa const &o) const {
2005 return mantissa != o.mantissa || power2 != o.power2;
2006 }
2007};

2559template <typename T>
2560fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 void
2561to_float(bool negative, adjusted_mantissa am, T &value) {
2562 using equiv_uint = equiv_uint_t<T>;
2563 equiv_uint word = equiv_uint(am.mantissa);
2564 word = equiv_uint(word | equiv_uint(am.power2)
2565 << binary_format<T>::mantissa_explicit_bits());
2566 word =
2567 equiv_uint(word | equiv_uint(negative) << binary_format<T>::sign_index());
2568#if FASTFLOAT_HAS_BIT_CAST
2569 value = std::bit_cast<T>(word);
2570#else
2571 ::memcpy(&value, &word, sizeof(T));
2572#endif
2573}

2600template <typename UC> static constexpr uint64_t int_cmp_zeros() {

2602 "Unsupported character size");

2604 : (sizeof(UC) == 2)
2605 ? (uint64_t(UC('0')) << 48 | uint64_t(UC('0')) << 32 |
2606 uint64_t(UC('0')) << 16 | UC('0'))
2607 : (uint64_t(UC('0')) << 32 | UC('0'));

2905// Next function can be micro-optimized, but compilers are entirely
2906// able to optimize it well.
2907template <typename UC>
2908fastfloat_really_inline constexpr bool is_integer(UC c) noexcept {
2909 return !(c > UC('9') || c < UC('0'));
2910}

2912fastfloat_really_inline constexpr uint64_t byteswap(uint64_t val) {
2913 return (val & 0xFF00000000000000) >> 56 | (val & 0x00FF000000000000) >> 40 |
2914 (val & 0x0000FF0000000000) >> 24 | (val & 0x000000FF00000000) >> 8 |
2915 (val & 0x00000000FF000000) << 8 | (val & 0x0000000000FF0000) << 24 |
2916 (val & 0x000000000000FF00) << 40 | (val & 0x00000000000000FF) << 56;
2917}
2918
2919// Read 8 UC into a u64. Truncates UC if not char.
2920template <typename UC>
2921fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 uint64_t
2922read8_to_u64(UC const *chars) {
2923 if (cpp20_and_in_constexpr() || !tinyobj_ff::is_same<UC, char>::value) {
2924 uint64_t val = 0;
2925 for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {
2926 val |= uint64_t(uint8_t(*chars)) << (i * 8);
2927 ++chars;
2928 }
2929 return val;
2930 }
2931 uint64_t val;
2932 ::memcpy(&val, chars, sizeof(uint64_t));
2933#if FASTFLOAT_IS_BIG_ENDIAN == 1
2934 // Need to read as-if the number was in little-endian order.
2935 val = byteswap(val);
2936#endif
2937 return val;
2938}

2942fastfloat_really_inline uint64_t simd_read8_to_u64(__m128i const data) {
2943 FASTFLOAT_SIMD_DISABLE_WARNINGS
2944 __m128i const packed = _mm_packus_epi16(data, data);
2945#ifdef FASTFLOAT_64BIT
2946 return uint64_t(_mm_cvtsi128_si64(packed));
2947#else
2948 uint64_t value;
2949 // Visual Studio + older versions of GCC don't support _mm_storeu_si64
2950 _mm_storel_epi64(reinterpret_cast<__m128i *>(&value), packed);
2951 return value;
2952#endif
2953 FASTFLOAT_SIMD_RESTORE_WARNINGS
2954}

2992// credit @aqrit
2993fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 uint32_t
2994parse_eight_digits_unrolled(uint64_t val) {
2995 uint64_t const mask = 0x000000FF000000FF;
2996 uint64_t const mul1 = 0x000F424000000064; // 100 + (1000000ULL << 32)
2997 uint64_t const mul2 = 0x0000271000000001; // 1 + (10000ULL << 32)
2998 val -= 0x3030303030303030;
2999 val = (val * 10) + (val >> 8); // val = (val * 2561) >> 8;
3000 val = (((val & mask) * mul1) + (((val >> 16) & mask) * mul2)) >> 32;
3001 return uint32_t(val);
3002}
3003
3004// Call this if chars are definitely 8 digits.
3005template <typename UC>
3006fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 uint32_t
3007parse_eight_digits_unrolled(UC const *chars) noexcept {
3008 if (cpp20_and_in_constexpr() || !has_simd_opt<UC>()) {
3009 return parse_eight_digits_unrolled(read8_to_u64(chars)); // truncation okay
3010 }
3011 return parse_eight_digits_unrolled(simd_read8_to_u64(chars));
3012}
3013
3014// credit @aqrit
3015fastfloat_really_inline constexpr bool
3016is_made_of_eight_digits_fast(uint64_t val) noexcept {
3017 return !((((val + 0x4646464646464646) | (val - 0x3030303030303030)) &
3018 0x8080808080808080));
3019}
3020
3021#ifdef FASTFLOAT_HAS_SIMD
3022
3023// Call this if chars might not be 8 digits.
3024// Using this style (instead of is_made_of_eight_digits_fast() then
3025// parse_eight_digits_unrolled()) ensures we don't load SIMD registers twice.
3026fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool
3027simd_parse_if_eight_digits_unrolled(char16_t const *chars,
3028 uint64_t &i) noexcept {
3029 if (cpp20_and_in_constexpr()) {
3030 return false;
3031 }
3032#ifdef FASTFLOAT_SSE2
3033 FASTFLOAT_SIMD_DISABLE_WARNINGS
3034 __m128i const data =
3035 _mm_loadu_si128(reinterpret_cast<__m128i const *>(chars));
3036
3037 // (x - '0') <= 9
3038 // http://0x80.pl/articles/simd-parsing-int-sequences.html
3039 __m128i const t0 = _mm_add_epi16(data, _mm_set1_epi16(32720));
3040 __m128i const t1 = _mm_cmpgt_epi16(t0, _mm_set1_epi16(-32759));
3041
3042 if (_mm_movemask_epi8(t1) == 0) {
3043 i = i * 100000000 + parse_eight_digits_unrolled(simd_read8_to_u64(data));
3044 return true;
3045 } else
3046 return false;
3047 FASTFLOAT_SIMD_RESTORE_WARNINGS
3048#elif defined(FASTFLOAT_NEON)
3049 FASTFLOAT_SIMD_DISABLE_WARNINGS
3050 uint16x8_t const data = vld1q_u16(reinterpret_cast<uint16_t const *>(chars));
3051
3052 // (x - '0') <= 9
3053 // http://0x80.pl/articles/simd-parsing-int-sequences.html
3054 uint16x8_t const t0 = vsubq_u16(data, vmovq_n_u16('0'));
3055 uint16x8_t const mask = vcltq_u16(t0, vmovq_n_u16('9' - '0' + 1));
3056
3057 if (vminvq_u16(mask) == 0xFFFF) {
3058 i = i * 100000000 + parse_eight_digits_unrolled(simd_read8_to_u64(data));
3059 return true;
3060 } else
3061 return false;
3062 FASTFLOAT_SIMD_RESTORE_WARNINGS
3063#else
3064 (void)chars;
3065 (void)i;
3066 return false;
3067#endif // FASTFLOAT_SSE2
3068}
3069
3070#endif // FASTFLOAT_HAS_SIMD

3073#if defined(_MSC_VER) && _MSC_VER <= 1900
3074template <typename UC>
3075#else
3076template <typename UC, FASTFLOAT_ENABLE_IF(!has_simd_opt<UC>()) = 0>
3077#endif
3078// dummy for compile
3079bool simd_parse_if_eight_digits_unrolled(UC const *, uint64_t &) {
3080 return 0;
3081}
3082
3083template <typename UC, FASTFLOAT_ENABLE_IF(!tinyobj_ff::is_same<UC, char>::value) = 0>
3084fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 void
3085loop_parse_if_eight_digits(UC const *&p, UC const *const pend, uint64_t &i) {
3086 if (!has_simd_opt<UC>()) {
3087 return;
3088 }
3089 while ((tinyobj_ff::distance(p, pend) >= 8) &&
3090 simd_parse_if_eight_digits_unrolled(
3091 p, i)) { // in rare cases, this will overflow, but that's ok
3092 p += 8;
3093 }
3094}
3095
3096fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 void
3097loop_parse_if_eight_digits(char const *&p, char const *const pend,
3098 uint64_t &i) {
3099 // optimizes better than parse_if_eight_digits_unrolled() for UC = char.
3100 while ((tinyobj_ff::distance(p, pend) >= 8) &&
3101 is_made_of_eight_digits_fast(read8_to_u64(p))) {
3102 i = i * 100000000 +
3103 parse_eight_digits_unrolled(read8_to_u64(
3104 p)); // in rare cases, this will overflow, but that's ok
3105 p += 8;
3106 }
3107}

3109enum class parse_error {
3110 no_error,
3111 // [JSON-only] The minus sign must be followed by an integer.
3112 missing_integer_after_sign,
3113 // A sign must be followed by an integer or dot.
3114 missing_integer_or_dot_after_sign,
3115 // [JSON-only] The integer part must not have leading zeros.
3116 leading_zeros_in_integer_part,
3117 // [JSON-only] The integer part must have at least one digit.
3118 no_digits_in_integer_part,
3119 // [JSON-only] If there is a decimal point, there must be digits in the
3120 // fractional part.
3121 no_digits_in_fractional_part,
3122 // The mantissa must have at least one digit.
3123 no_digits_in_mantissa,
3124 // Scientific notation requires an exponential part.
3125 missing_exponential_part,
3126};
3127
3128template <typename UC> struct parsed_number_string_t {
3129 int64_t exponent{0};
3130 uint64_t mantissa{0};
3131 UC const *lastmatch{nullptr};
3132 bool negative{false};
3133 bool valid{false};
3134 bool too_many_digits{false};
3135 // contains the range of the significant digits
3136 span<UC const> integer{}; // non-nullable
3137 span<UC const> fraction{}; // nullable
3138 parse_error error{parse_error::no_error};
3139};
3140
3141using byte_span = span<char const>;
3142using parsed_number_string = parsed_number_string_t<char>;
3143
3144template <typename UC>
3145fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 parsed_number_string_t<UC>
3146report_parse_error(UC const *p, parse_error error) {
3147 parsed_number_string_t<UC> answer;
3148 answer.valid = false;
3149 answer.lastmatch = p;
3150 answer.error = error;
3151 return answer;
3152}
3153
3154// Assuming that you use no more than 19 digits, this will
3155// parse an ASCII string.
3156template <bool basic_json_fmt, typename UC>
3157fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 parsed_number_string_t<UC>
3158parse_number_string(UC const *p, UC const *pend,
3159 parse_options_t<UC> options) noexcept {
3160 chars_format const fmt = detail::adjust_for_feature_macros(options.format);
3161 UC const decimal_point = options.decimal_point;
3162
3163 parsed_number_string_t<UC> answer;
3164 answer.valid = false;
3165 answer.too_many_digits = false;
3166 // assume p < pend, so dereference without checks;
3167 answer.negative = (*p == UC('-'));
3168 // C++17 20.19.3.(7.1) explicitly forbids '+' sign here
3169 if ((*p == UC('-')) || (uint64_t(fmt & chars_format::allow_leading_plus) &&
3170 !basic_json_fmt && *p == UC('+'))) {
3171 ++p;
3172 if (p == pend) {
3173 return report_parse_error<UC>(
3174 p, parse_error::missing_integer_or_dot_after_sign);
3175 }
3176 FASTFLOAT_IF_CONSTEXPR17(basic_json_fmt) {
3177 if (!is_integer(*p)) { // a sign must be followed by an integer
3178 return report_parse_error<UC>(p,
3179 parse_error::missing_integer_after_sign);
3180 }
3181 }
3182 else {
3183 if (!is_integer(*p) &&
3184 (*p !=
3185 decimal_point)) { // a sign must be followed by an integer or the dot
3186 return report_parse_error<UC>(
3187 p, parse_error::missing_integer_or_dot_after_sign);
3188 }
3189 }
3190 }
3191 UC const *const start_digits = p;
3192
3193 uint64_t i = 0; // an unsigned int avoids signed overflows (which are bad)
3194
3195 while ((p != pend) && is_integer(*p)) {
3196 // a multiplication by 10 is cheaper than an arbitrary integer
3197 // multiplication
3198 i = 10 * i +
3199 uint64_t(*p -
3200 UC('0')); // might overflow, we will handle the overflow later
3201 ++p;
3202 }
3203 UC const *const end_of_integer_part = p;
3204 int64_t digit_count = int64_t(end_of_integer_part - start_digits);
3205 answer.integer = span<UC const>(start_digits, size_t(digit_count));
3206 FASTFLOAT_IF_CONSTEXPR17(basic_json_fmt) {
3207 // at least 1 digit in integer part, without leading zeros
3208 if (digit_count == 0) {
3209 return report_parse_error<UC>(p, parse_error::no_digits_in_integer_part);
3210 }
3211 if ((start_digits[0] == UC('0') && digit_count > 1)) {
3212 return report_parse_error<UC>(start_digits,
3213 parse_error::leading_zeros_in_integer_part);
3214 }
3215 }
3216
3217 int64_t exponent = 0;
3218 bool const has_decimal_point = (p != pend) && (*p == decimal_point);
3219 if (has_decimal_point) {
3220 ++p;
3221 UC const *before = p;
3222 // can occur at most twice without overflowing, but let it occur more, since
3223 // for integers with many digits, digit parsing is the primary bottleneck.
3224 loop_parse_if_eight_digits(p, pend, i);
3225
3226 while ((p != pend) && is_integer(*p)) {
3227 uint8_t digit = uint8_t(*p - UC('0'));
3228 ++p;
3229 i = i * 10 + digit; // in rare cases, this will overflow, but that's ok
3230 }
3231 exponent = before - p;
3232 answer.fraction = span<UC const>(before, size_t(p - before));
3233 digit_count -= exponent;
3234 }
3235 FASTFLOAT_IF_CONSTEXPR17(basic_json_fmt) {
3236 // at least 1 digit in fractional part
3237 if (has_decimal_point && exponent == 0) {
3238 return report_parse_error<UC>(p,
3239 parse_error::no_digits_in_fractional_part);
3240 }
3241 }
3242 else if (digit_count == 0) { // we must have encountered at least one integer!
3243 return report_parse_error<UC>(p, parse_error::no_digits_in_mantissa);
3244 }
3245 int64_t exp_number = 0; // explicit exponential part
3246 if ((uint64_t(fmt & chars_format::scientific) && (p != pend) &&
3247 ((UC('e') == *p) || (UC('E') == *p))) ||
3248 (uint64_t(fmt & detail::basic_fortran_fmt) && (p != pend) &&
3249 ((UC('+') == *p) || (UC('-') == *p) || (UC('d') == *p) ||
3250 (UC('D') == *p)))) {
3251 UC const *location_of_e = p;
3252 if ((UC('e') == *p) || (UC('E') == *p) || (UC('d') == *p) ||
3253 (UC('D') == *p)) {
3254 ++p;
3255 }
3256 bool neg_exp = false;
3257 if ((p != pend) && (UC('-') == *p)) {
3258 neg_exp = true;
3259 ++p;
3260 } else if ((p != pend) &&
3261 (UC('+') ==
3262 *p)) { // '+' on exponent is allowed by C++17 20.19.3.(7.1)
3263 ++p;
3264 }
3265 if ((p == pend) || !is_integer(*p)) {
3266 if (!uint64_t(fmt & chars_format::fixed)) {
3267 // The exponential part is invalid for scientific notation, so it must
3268 // be a trailing token for fixed notation. However, fixed notation is
3269 // disabled, so report a scientific notation error.
3270 return report_parse_error<UC>(p, parse_error::missing_exponential_part);
3271 }
3272 // Otherwise, we will be ignoring the 'e'.
3273 p = location_of_e;
3274 } else {
3275 while ((p != pend) && is_integer(*p)) {
3276 uint8_t digit = uint8_t(*p - UC('0'));
3277 if (exp_number < 0x10000000) {
3278 exp_number = 10 * exp_number + digit;
3279 }
3280 ++p;
3281 }
3282 if (neg_exp) {
3283 exp_number = -exp_number;
3284 }
3285 exponent += exp_number;
3286 }
3287 } else {
3288 // If it scientific and not fixed, we have to bail out.
3289 if (uint64_t(fmt & chars_format::scientific) &&
3290 !uint64_t(fmt & chars_format::fixed)) {
3291 return report_parse_error<UC>(p, parse_error::missing_exponential_part);
3292 }
3293 }
3294 answer.lastmatch = p;
3295 answer.valid = true;
3296
3297 // If we frequently had to deal with long strings of digits,
3298 // we could extend our code by using a 128-bit integer instead
3299 // of a 64-bit integer. However, this is uncommon.
3300 //
3301 // We can deal with up to 19 digits.
3302 if (digit_count > 19) { // this is uncommon
3303 // It is possible that the integer had an overflow.
3304 // We have to handle the case where we have 0.0000somenumber.
3305 // We need to be mindful of the case where we only have zeroes...
3306 // E.g., 0.000000000...000.
3307 UC const *start = start_digits;
3308 while ((start != pend) && (*start == UC('0') || *start == decimal_point)) {
3309 if (*start == UC('0')) {
3310 digit_count--;
3311 }
3312 start++;
3313 }
3314
3315 if (digit_count > 19) {
3316 answer.too_many_digits = true;
3317 // Let us start again, this time, avoiding overflows.
3318 // We don't need to check if is_integer, since we use the
3319 // pre-tokenized spans from above.
3320 i = 0;
3321 p = answer.integer.ptr;
3322 UC const *int_end = p + answer.integer.len();
3323 uint64_t const minimal_nineteen_digit_integer{1000000000000000000};
3324 while ((i < minimal_nineteen_digit_integer) && (p != int_end)) {
3325 i = i * 10 + uint64_t(*p - UC('0'));
3326 ++p;
3327 }
3328 if (i >= minimal_nineteen_digit_integer) { // We have a big integers
3329 exponent = end_of_integer_part - p + exp_number;
3330 } else { // We have a value with a fractional component.
3331 p = answer.fraction.ptr;
3332 UC const *frac_end = p + answer.fraction.len();
3333 while ((i < minimal_nineteen_digit_integer) && (p != frac_end)) {
3334 i = i * 10 + uint64_t(*p - UC('0'));
3335 ++p;
3336 }
3337 exponent = answer.fraction.ptr - p + exp_number;
3338 }
3339 // We have now corrected both exponent and i, to a truncated value
3340 }
3341 }
3342 answer.exponent = exponent;
3343 answer.mantissa = i;
3344 return answer;
3345}
3346
3347template <typename T, typename UC>
3348fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 from_chars_result_t<UC>
3349parse_int_string(UC const *p, UC const *pend, T &value,
3350 parse_options_t<UC> options) {
3351 chars_format const fmt = detail::adjust_for_feature_macros(options.format);
3352 int const base = options.base;
3353
3354 from_chars_result_t<UC> answer;
3355
3356 UC const *const first = p;
3357
3358 bool const negative = (*p == UC('-'));
3359#ifdef FASTFLOAT_VISUAL_STUDIO
3360#pragma warning(push)
3361#pragma warning(disable : 4127)
3362#endif
3363 if (!tinyobj_ff::is_signed<T>::value && negative) {
3364#ifdef FASTFLOAT_VISUAL_STUDIO
3365#pragma warning(pop)
3366#endif
3367 answer.ec = tinyobj_ff::ff_errc::invalid_argument;
3368 answer.ptr = first;
3369 return answer;
3370 }
3371 if ((*p == UC('-')) ||
3372 (uint64_t(fmt & chars_format::allow_leading_plus) && (*p == UC('+')))) {
3373 ++p;
3374 }
3375
3376 UC const *const start_num = p;
3377
3378 while (p != pend && *p == UC('0')) {
3379 ++p;
3380 }
3381
3382 bool const has_leading_zeros = p > start_num;
3383
3384 UC const *const start_digits = p;
3385
3386 uint64_t i = 0;
3387 if (base == 10) {
3388 loop_parse_if_eight_digits(p, pend, i); // use SIMD if possible
3389 }
3390 while (p != pend) {
3391 uint8_t digit = ch_to_digit(*p);
3392 if (digit >= base) {
3393 break;
3394 }
3395 i = uint64_t(base) * i + digit; // might overflow, check this later
3396 p++;
3397 }
3398
3399 size_t digit_count = size_t(p - start_digits);
3400
3401 if (digit_count == 0) {
3402 if (has_leading_zeros) {
3403 value = 0;
3404 answer.ec = tinyobj_ff::ff_errc();
3405 answer.ptr = p;
3406 } else {
3407 answer.ec = tinyobj_ff::ff_errc::invalid_argument;
3408 answer.ptr = first;
3409 }
3410 return answer;
3411 }
3412
3413 answer.ptr = p;
3414
3415 // check u64 overflow
3416 size_t max_digits = max_digits_u64(base);
3417 if (digit_count > max_digits) {
3418 answer.ec = tinyobj_ff::ff_errc::result_out_of_range;
3419 return answer;
3420 }
3421 // this check can be eliminated for all other types, but they will all require
3422 // a max_digits(base) equivalent
3423 if (digit_count == max_digits && i < min_safe_u64(base)) {
3424 answer.ec = tinyobj_ff::ff_errc::result_out_of_range;
3425 return answer;
3426 }
3427
3428 // check other types overflow
3429 if (!tinyobj_ff::is_same<T, uint64_t>::value) {
3430 if (i > uint64_t(std::numeric_limits<T>::max()) + uint64_t(negative)) {
3431 answer.ec = tinyobj_ff::ff_errc::result_out_of_range;
3432 return answer;
3433 }
3434 }
3435
3436 if (negative) {
3437#ifdef FASTFLOAT_VISUAL_STUDIO
3438#pragma warning(push)
3439#pragma warning(disable : 4146)
3440#endif
3441 // this weird workaround is required because:
3442 // - converting unsigned to signed when its value is greater than signed max
3443 // is UB pre-C++23.
3444 // - reinterpret_casting (~i + 1) would work, but it is not constexpr
3445 // this is always optimized into a neg instruction (note: T is an integer
3446 // type)
3447 value = T(-std::numeric_limits<T>::max() -
3448 T(i - uint64_t(std::numeric_limits<T>::max())));
3449#ifdef FASTFLOAT_VISUAL_STUDIO
3450#pragma warning(pop)
3451#endif
3452 } else {
3453 value = T(i);
3454 }
3455
3456 answer.ec = tinyobj_ff::ff_errc();
3457 return answer;
3458}

4172#define FASTFLOAT_DECIMAL_TO_BINARY_H

4174#include <cmath>

4176#include <cstring>

4178namespace fast_float {

4180// This will compute or rather approximate w * 5**q and return a pair of 64-bit
4181// words approximating the result, with the "high" part corresponding to the
4182// most significant bits and the low part corresponding to the least significant
4183// bits.
4184//
4185template <int bit_precision>
4186fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 value128
4187compute_product_approximation(int64_t q, uint64_t w) {
4188 int const index = 2 * int(q - powers::smallest_power_of_five);
4189 // For small values of q, e.g., q in [0,27], the answer is always exact
4190 // because The line value128 firstproduct = full_multiplication(w,
4191 // power_of_five_128[index]); gives the exact answer.
4192 value128 firstproduct =
4193 full_multiplication(w, powers::power_of_five_128[index]);
4194 static_assert((bit_precision >= 0) && (bit_precision <= 64),
4195 " precision should be in (0,64]");
4196 constexpr uint64_t precision_mask =
4197 (bit_precision < 64) ? (uint64_t(0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) >> bit_precision)
4198 : uint64_t(0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF);
4199 if ((firstproduct.high & precision_mask) ==
4200 precision_mask) { // could further guard with (lower + w < lower)
4201 // regarding the second product, we only need secondproduct.high, but our
4202 // expectation is that the compiler will optimize this extra work away if
4203 // needed.
4204 value128 secondproduct =
4205 full_multiplication(w, powers::power_of_five_128[index + 1]);
4206 firstproduct.low += secondproduct.high;
4207 if (secondproduct.high > firstproduct.low) {
4208 firstproduct.high++;
4209 }
4210 }
4211 return firstproduct;
4212}
4213
4214namespace detail {
4230constexpr fastfloat_really_inline int32_t power(int32_t q) noexcept {
4231 return (((152170 + 65536) * q) >> 16) + 63;
4232}
4233} // namespace detail
4234
4235// create an adjusted mantissa, biased by the invalid power2
4236// for significant digits already multiplied by 10 ** q.
4237template <typename binary>
4238fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 adjusted_mantissa
4239compute_error_scaled(int64_t q, uint64_t w, int lz) noexcept {
4240 int hilz = int(w >> 63) ^ 1;
4241 adjusted_mantissa answer;
4242 answer.mantissa = w << hilz;
4243 int bias = binary::mantissa_explicit_bits() - binary::minimum_exponent();
4244 answer.power2 = int32_t(detail::power(int32_t(q)) + bias - hilz - lz - 62 +
4245 invalid_am_bias);
4246 return answer;
4247}
4248
4249// w * 10 ** q, without rounding the representation up.
4250// the power2 in the exponent will be adjusted by invalid_am_bias.
4251template <typename binary>
4252fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 adjusted_mantissa
4253compute_error(int64_t q, uint64_t w) noexcept {
4254 int lz = leading_zeroes(w);
4255 w <<= lz;
4256 value128 product =
4257 compute_product_approximation<binary::mantissa_explicit_bits() + 3>(q, w);
4258 return compute_error_scaled<binary>(q, product.high, lz);
4259}
4260
4261// Computers w * 10 ** q.
4262// The returned value should be a valid number that simply needs to be
4263// packed. However, in some very rare cases, the computation will fail. In such
4264// cases, we return an adjusted_mantissa with a negative power of 2: the caller
4265// should recompute in such cases.
4266template <typename binary>
4267fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 adjusted_mantissa
4268compute_float(int64_t q, uint64_t w) noexcept {
4269 adjusted_mantissa answer;
4270 if ((w == 0) || (q < binary::smallest_power_of_ten())) {
4271 answer.power2 = 0;
4272 answer.mantissa = 0;
4273 // result should be zero
4274 return answer;
4275 }
4276 if (q > binary::largest_power_of_ten()) {
4277 // we want to get infinity:
4278 answer.power2 = binary::infinite_power();
4279 answer.mantissa = 0;
4280 return answer;
4281 }
4282 // At this point in time q is in [powers::smallest_power_of_five,
4283 // powers::largest_power_of_five].
4284
4285 // We want the most significant bit of i to be 1. Shift if needed.
4286 int lz = leading_zeroes(w);
4287 w <<= lz;
4288
4289 // The required precision is binary::mantissa_explicit_bits() + 3 because
4290 // 1. We need the implicit bit
4291 // 2. We need an extra bit for rounding purposes
4292 // 3. We might lose a bit due to the "upperbit" routine (result too small,
4293 // requiring a shift)
4294
4295 value128 product =
4296 compute_product_approximation<binary::mantissa_explicit_bits() + 3>(q, w);
4297 // The computed 'product' is always sufficient.
4298 // Mathematical proof:
4299 // Noble Mushtak and Daniel Lemire, Fast Number Parsing Without Fallback (to
4300 // appear) See script/mushtak_lemire.py
4301
4302 // The "compute_product_approximation" function can be slightly slower than a
4303 // branchless approach: value128 product = compute_product(q, w); but in
4304 // practice, we can win big with the compute_product_approximation if its
4305 // additional branch is easily predicted. Which is best is data specific.
4306 int upperbit = int(product.high >> 63);
4307 int shift = upperbit + 64 - binary::mantissa_explicit_bits() - 3;
4308
4309 answer.mantissa = product.high >> shift;
4310
4311 answer.power2 = int32_t(detail::power(int32_t(q)) + upperbit - lz -
4312 binary::minimum_exponent());
4313 if (answer.power2 <= 0) { // we have a subnormal?
4314 // Here have that answer.power2 <= 0 so -answer.power2 >= 0
4315 if (-answer.power2 + 1 >=
4316 64) { // if we have more than 64 bits below the minimum exponent, you
4317 // have a zero for sure.
4318 answer.power2 = 0;
4319 answer.mantissa = 0;
4320 // result should be zero
4321 return answer;
4322 }
4323 // next line is safe because -answer.power2 + 1 < 64
4324 answer.mantissa >>= -answer.power2 + 1;
4325 // Thankfully, we can't have both "round-to-even" and subnormals because
4326 // "round-to-even" only occurs for powers close to 0 in the 32-bit and
4327 // and 64-bit case (with no more than 19 digits).
4328 answer.mantissa += (answer.mantissa & 1); // round up
4329 answer.mantissa >>= 1;
4330 // There is a weird scenario where we don't have a subnormal but just.
4331 // Suppose we start with 2.2250738585072013e-308, we end up
4332 // with 0x3fffffffffffff x 2^-1023-53 which is technically subnormal
4333 // whereas 0x40000000000000 x 2^-1023-53 is normal. Now, we need to round
4334 // up 0x3fffffffffffff x 2^-1023-53 and once we do, we are no longer
4335 // subnormal, but we can only know this after rounding.
4336 // So we only declare a subnormal if we are smaller than the threshold.
4337 answer.power2 =
4338 (answer.mantissa < (uint64_t(1) << binary::mantissa_explicit_bits()))
4339 ? 0
4340 : 1;
4341 return answer;
4342 }
4343
4344 // usually, we round *up*, but if we fall right in between and and we have an
4345 // even basis, we need to round down
4346 // We are only concerned with the cases where 5**q fits in single 64-bit word.
4347 if ((product.low <= 1) && (q >= binary::min_exponent_round_to_even()) &&
4348 (q <= binary::max_exponent_round_to_even()) &&
4349 ((answer.mantissa & 3) == 1)) { // we may fall between two floats!
4350 // To be in-between two floats we need that in doing
4351 // answer.mantissa = product.high >> (upperbit + 64 -
4352 // binary::mantissa_explicit_bits() - 3);
4353 // ... we dropped out only zeroes. But if this happened, then we can go
4354 // back!!!
4355 if ((answer.mantissa << shift) == product.high) {
4356 answer.mantissa &= ~uint64_t(1); // flip it so that we do not round up
4357 }
4358 }
4359
4360 answer.mantissa += (answer.mantissa & 1); // round up
4361 answer.mantissa >>= 1;
4362 if (answer.mantissa >= (uint64_t(2) << binary::mantissa_explicit_bits())) {
4363 answer.mantissa = (uint64_t(1) << binary::mantissa_explicit_bits());
4364 answer.power2++; // undo previous addition
4365 }
4366
4367 answer.mantissa &= ~(uint64_t(1) << binary::mantissa_explicit_bits());
4368 if (answer.power2 >= binary::infinite_power()) { // infinity
4369 answer.power2 = binary::infinite_power();
4370 answer.mantissa = 0;
4371 }
4372 return answer;
4373}

4379#ifndef FASTFLOAT_BIGINT_H
4380#define FASTFLOAT_BIGINT_H
4381
4382#include <cstring>
4383
4384
4385namespace fast_float {
4386
4387// the limb width: we want efficient multiplication of double the bits in
4388// limb, or for 64-bit limbs, at least 64-bit multiplication where we can
4389// extract the high and low parts efficiently. this is every 64-bit
4390// architecture except for sparc, which emulates 128-bit multiplication.
4391// we might have platforms where `CHAR_BIT` is not 8, so let's avoid
4392// doing `8 * sizeof(limb)`.
4393#if defined(FASTFLOAT_64BIT) && !defined(__sparc)
4394#define FASTFLOAT_64BIT_LIMB 1
4395typedef uint64_t limb;
4396constexpr size_t limb_bits = 64;
4397#else
4398#define FASTFLOAT_32BIT_LIMB
4399typedef uint32_t limb;
4400constexpr size_t limb_bits = 32;
4401#endif
4402
4403typedef span<limb> limb_span;
4404
4405// number of bits in a bigint. this needs to be at least the number
4406// of bits required to store the largest bigint, which is
4407// `log2(10**(digits + max_exp))`, or `log2(10**(767 + 342))`, or
4408// ~3600 bits, so we round to 4000.
4409constexpr size_t bigint_bits = 4000;
4410constexpr size_t bigint_limbs = bigint_bits / limb_bits;
4411
4412// vector-like type that is allocated on the stack. the entire
4413// buffer is pre-allocated, and only the length changes.
4414template <uint16_t size> struct stackvec {
4415 limb data[size];
4416 // we never need more than 150 limbs
4417 uint16_t length{0};
4418
4419 stackvec() = default;
4420 stackvec(stackvec const &) = delete;
4421 stackvec &operator=(stackvec const &) = delete;
4422 stackvec(stackvec &&) = delete;
4423 stackvec &operator=(stackvec &&other) = delete;
4424
4425 // create stack vector from existing limb span.
4426 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 stackvec(limb_span s) {
4427 FASTFLOAT_ASSERT(try_extend(s));
4428 }
4429
4430 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 limb &operator[](size_t index) noexcept {
4431 FASTFLOAT_DEBUG_ASSERT(index < length);
4432 return data[index];
4433 }
4434
4435 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 const limb &operator[](size_t index) const noexcept {
4436 FASTFLOAT_DEBUG_ASSERT(index < length);
4437 return data[index];
4438 }
4439
4440 // index from the end of the container
4441 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 const limb &rindex(size_t index) const noexcept {
4442 FASTFLOAT_DEBUG_ASSERT(index < length);
4443 size_t rindex = length - index - 1;
4444 return data[rindex];
4445 }
4446
4447 // set the length, without bounds checking.
4448 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 void set_len(size_t len) noexcept {
4449 length = uint16_t(len);
4450 }
4451
4452 constexpr size_t len() const noexcept { return length; }
4453
4454 constexpr bool is_empty() const noexcept { return length == 0; }
4455
4456 constexpr size_t capacity() const noexcept { return size; }
4457
4458 // append item to vector, without bounds checking
4459 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 void push_unchecked(limb value) noexcept {
4460 data[length] = value;
4461 length++;
4462 }
4463
4464 // append item to vector, returning if item was added
4465 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 bool try_push(limb value) noexcept {
4466 if (len() < capacity()) {
4467 push_unchecked(value);
4468 return true;
4469 } else {
4470 return false;
4471 }
4472 }
4473
4474 // add items to the vector, from a span, without bounds checking
4475 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 void extend_unchecked(limb_span s) noexcept {
4476 limb *ptr = data + length;
4477 tinyobj_ff::copy_n(s.ptr, s.len(), ptr);
4478 set_len(len() + s.len());
4479 }
4480
4481 // try to add items to the vector, returning if items were added
4482 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool try_extend(limb_span s) noexcept {
4483 if (len() + s.len() <= capacity()) {
4484 extend_unchecked(s);
4485 return true;
4486 } else {
4487 return false;
4488 }
4489 }
4490
4491 // resize the vector, without bounds checking
4492 // if the new size is longer than the vector, assign value to each
4493 // appended item.
4494 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20
4495 void resize_unchecked(size_t new_len, limb value) noexcept {
4496 if (new_len > len()) {
4497 size_t count = new_len - len();
4498 limb *first = data + len();
4499 limb *last = first + count;
4500 tinyobj_ff::fill(first, last, value);
4501 set_len(new_len);
4502 } else {
4503 set_len(new_len);
4504 }
4505 }
4506
4507 // try to resize the vector, returning if the vector was resized.
4508 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool try_resize(size_t new_len, limb value) noexcept {
4509 if (new_len > capacity()) {
4510 return false;
4511 } else {
4512 resize_unchecked(new_len, value);
4513 return true;
4514 }
4515 }
4516
4517 // check if any limbs are non-zero after the given index.
4518 // this needs to be done in reverse order, since the index
4519 // is relative to the most significant limbs.
4520 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 bool nonzero(size_t index) const noexcept {
4521 while (index < len()) {
4522 if (rindex(index) != 0) {
4523 return true;
4524 }
4525 index++;
4526 }
4527 return false;
4528 }
4529
4530 // normalize the big integer, so most-significant zero limbs are removed.
4531 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 void normalize() noexcept {
4532 while (len() > 0 && rindex(0) == 0) {
4533 length--;
4534 }
4535 }
4536};
4537
4538fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR14 uint64_t
4539empty_hi64(bool &truncated) noexcept {
4540 truncated = false;
4541 return 0;
4542}
4543
4544fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 uint64_t
4545uint64_hi64(uint64_t r0, bool &truncated) noexcept {
4546 truncated = false;
4547 int shl = leading_zeroes(r0);
4548 return r0 << shl;
4549}
4550
4551fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 uint64_t
4552uint64_hi64(uint64_t r0, uint64_t r1, bool &truncated) noexcept {
4553 int shl = leading_zeroes(r0);
4554 if (shl == 0) {
4555 truncated = r1 != 0;
4556 return r0;
4557 } else {
4558 int shr = 64 - shl;
4559 truncated = (r1 << shl) != 0;
4560 return (r0 << shl) | (r1 >> shr);
4561 }
4562}
4563
4564fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 uint64_t
4565uint32_hi64(uint32_t r0, bool &truncated) noexcept {
4566 return uint64_hi64(r0, truncated);
4567}
4568
4569fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 uint64_t
4570uint32_hi64(uint32_t r0, uint32_t r1, bool &truncated) noexcept {
4571 uint64_t x0 = r0;
4572 uint64_t x1 = r1;
4573 return uint64_hi64((x0 << 32) | x1, truncated);
4574}
4575
4576fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 uint64_t
4577uint32_hi64(uint32_t r0, uint32_t r1, uint32_t r2, bool &truncated) noexcept {
4578 uint64_t x0 = r0;
4579 uint64_t x1 = r1;
4580 uint64_t x2 = r2;
4581 return uint64_hi64(x0, (x1 << 32) | x2, truncated);
4582}
4583
4584// add two small integers, checking for overflow.
4585// we want an efficient operation. for msvc, where
4586// we don't have built-in intrinsics, this is still
4587// pretty fast.
4588fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 limb
4589scalar_add(limb x, limb y, bool &overflow) noexcept {
4590 limb z;
4591// gcc and clang
4592#if defined(__has_builtin)
4593#if __has_builtin(__builtin_add_overflow)
4594 if (!cpp20_and_in_constexpr()) {
4595 overflow = __builtin_add_overflow(x, y, &z);
4596 return z;
4597 }
4598#endif
4599#endif
4600
4601 // generic, this still optimizes correctly on MSVC.
4602 z = x + y;
4603 overflow = z < x;
4604 return z;
4605}
4606
4607// multiply two small integers, getting both the high and low bits.
4608fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 limb
4609scalar_mul(limb x, limb y, limb &carry) noexcept {
4610#ifdef FASTFLOAT_64BIT_LIMB
4611#if defined(__SIZEOF_INT128__)
4612 // GCC and clang both define it as an extension.
4613 __uint128_t z = __uint128_t(x) * __uint128_t(y) + __uint128_t(carry);
4614 carry = limb(z >> limb_bits);
4615 return limb(z);
4616#else
4617 // fallback, no native 128-bit integer multiplication with carry.
4618 // on msvc, this optimizes identically, somehow.
4619 value128 z = full_multiplication(x, y);
4620 bool overflow;
4621 z.low = scalar_add(z.low, carry, overflow);
4622 z.high += uint64_t(overflow); // cannot overflow
4623 carry = z.high;
4624 return z.low;
4625#endif
4626#else
4627 uint64_t z = uint64_t(x) * uint64_t(y) + uint64_t(carry);
4628 carry = limb(z >> limb_bits);
4629 return limb(z);
4630#endif
4631}
4632
4633// add scalar value to bigint starting from offset.
4634// used in grade school multiplication
4635template <uint16_t size>
4636inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool small_add_from(stackvec<size> &vec, limb y,
4637 size_t start) noexcept {
4638 size_t index = start;
4639 limb carry = y;
4640 bool overflow;
4641 while (carry != 0 && index < vec.len()) {
4642 vec[index] = scalar_add(vec[index], carry, overflow);
4643 carry = limb(overflow);
4644 index += 1;
4645 }
4646 if (carry != 0) {
4647 FASTFLOAT_TRY(vec.try_push(carry));
4648 }
4649 return true;
4650}
4651
4652// add scalar value to bigint.
4653template <uint16_t size>
4654fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool
4655small_add(stackvec<size> &vec, limb y) noexcept {
4656 return small_add_from(vec, y, 0);
4657}
4658
4659// multiply bigint by scalar value.
4660template <uint16_t size>
4661inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool small_mul(stackvec<size> &vec,
4662 limb y) noexcept {
4663 limb carry = 0;
4664 for (size_t index = 0; index < vec.len(); index++) {
4665 vec[index] = scalar_mul(vec[index], y, carry);
4666 }
4667 if (carry != 0) {
4668 FASTFLOAT_TRY(vec.try_push(carry));
4669 }
4670 return true;
4671}
4672
4673// add bigint to bigint starting from index.
4674// used in grade school multiplication
4675template <uint16_t size>
4676FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool large_add_from(stackvec<size> &x, limb_span y,
4677 size_t start) noexcept {
4678 // the effective x buffer is from `xstart..x.len()`, so exit early
4679 // if we can't get that current range.
4680 if (x.len() < start || y.len() > x.len() - start) {
4681 FASTFLOAT_TRY(x.try_resize(y.len() + start, 0));
4682 }
4683
4684 bool carry = false;
4685 for (size_t index = 0; index < y.len(); index++) {
4686 limb xi = x[index + start];
4687 limb yi = y[index];
4688 bool c1 = false;
4689 bool c2 = false;
4690 xi = scalar_add(xi, yi, c1);
4691 if (carry) {
4692 xi = scalar_add(xi, 1, c2);
4693 }
4694 x[index + start] = xi;
4695 carry = c1 | c2;
4696 }
4697
4698 // handle overflow
4699 if (carry) {
4700 FASTFLOAT_TRY(small_add_from(x, 1, y.len() + start));
4701 }
4702 return true;
4703}
4704
4705// add bigint to bigint.
4706template <uint16_t size>
4707fastfloat_really_inline FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool
4708large_add_from(stackvec<size> &x, limb_span y) noexcept {
4709 return large_add_from(x, y, 0);
4710}
4711
4712// grade-school multiplication algorithm
4713template <uint16_t size>
4714FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool long_mul(stackvec<size> &x, limb_span y) noexcept {
4715 limb_span xs = limb_span(x.data, x.len());
4716 stackvec<size> z(xs);
4717 limb_span zs = limb_span(z.data, z.len());
4718
4719 if (y.len() != 0) {
4720 limb y0 = y[0];
4721 FASTFLOAT_TRY(small_mul(x, y0));
4722 for (size_t index = 1; index < y.len(); index++) {
4723 limb yi = y[index];
4724 stackvec<size> zi;
4725 if (yi != 0) {
4726 // re-use the same buffer throughout
4727 zi.set_len(0);
4728 FASTFLOAT_TRY(zi.try_extend(zs));
4729 FASTFLOAT_TRY(small_mul(zi, yi));
4730 limb_span zis = limb_span(zi.data, zi.len());
4731 FASTFLOAT_TRY(large_add_from(x, zis, index));
4732 }
4733 }
4734 }
4735
4736 x.normalize();
4737 return true;
4738}
4739
4740// grade-school multiplication algorithm
4741template <uint16_t size>
4742FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool large_mul(stackvec<size> &x, limb_span y) noexcept {
4743 if (y.len() == 1) {
4744 FASTFLOAT_TRY(small_mul(x, y[0]));
4745 } else {
4746 FASTFLOAT_TRY(long_mul(x, y));
4747 }
4748 return true;
4749}

4753 static constexpr uint64_t small_power_of_5[] = {

4767 1220703125UL,

4769 30517578125UL,

4771 762939453125UL,
4772 3814697265625UL,
4773 19073486328125UL,
4774 95367431640625UL,
4775 476837158203125UL,
4776 2384185791015625UL,
4777 11920928955078125UL,
4778 59604644775390625UL,

4786 10482974169319127550UL, 198276706040285095UL};
4787#else
4788 constexpr static limb large_power_of_5[] = {
4789 4279965485U, 329373468U, 4020270615U, 2137533757U, 4287402176U,

4794#if FASTFLOAT_DETAIL_MUST_DEFINE_CONSTEXPR_VARIABLE
4795
4796template <typename T> constexpr uint32_t pow5_tables<T>::large_step;
4797
4798template <typename T> constexpr uint64_t pow5_tables<T>::small_power_of_5[];
4799
4800template <typename T> constexpr limb pow5_tables<T>::large_power_of_5[];

4803
4804// big integer type. implements a small subset of big integer
4805// arithmetic, using simple algorithms since asymptotically
4806// faster algorithms are slower for a small number of limbs.
4807// all operations assume the big-integer is normalized.
4808struct bigint : pow5_tables<> {
4809 // storage of the limbs, in little-endian order.
4810 stackvec<bigint_limbs> vec;
4811
4812 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bigint() : vec() {}
4813
4814 bigint(bigint const &) = delete;
4815 bigint &operator=(bigint const &) = delete;
4816 bigint(bigint &&) = delete;
4817 bigint &operator=(bigint &&other) = delete;
4818
4819 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bigint(uint64_t value) : vec() {
4820#ifdef FASTFLOAT_64BIT_LIMB
4821 vec.push_unchecked(value);
4822#else
4823 vec.push_unchecked(uint32_t(value));
4824 vec.push_unchecked(uint32_t(value >> 32));
4825#endif
4826 vec.normalize();
4827 }
4828
4829 // get the high 64 bits from the vector, and if bits were truncated.
4830 // this is to get the significant digits for the float.
4831 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 uint64_t hi64(bool &truncated) const noexcept {
4832#ifdef FASTFLOAT_64BIT_LIMB
4833 if (vec.len() == 0) {
4834 return empty_hi64(truncated);
4835 } else if (vec.len() == 1) {
4836 return uint64_hi64(vec.rindex(0), truncated);
4837 } else {
4838 uint64_t result = uint64_hi64(vec.rindex(0), vec.rindex(1), truncated);
4839 truncated |= vec.nonzero(2);
4840 return result;
4841 }
4842#else
4843 if (vec.len() == 0) {
4844 return empty_hi64(truncated);
4845 } else if (vec.len() == 1) {
4846 return uint32_hi64(vec.rindex(0), truncated);
4847 } else if (vec.len() == 2) {
4848 return uint32_hi64(vec.rindex(0), vec.rindex(1), truncated);
4849 } else {
4850 uint64_t result =
4851 uint32_hi64(vec.rindex(0), vec.rindex(1), vec.rindex(2), truncated);
4852 truncated |= vec.nonzero(3);
4853 return result;
4854 }
4855#endif
4856 }
4857
4858 // compare two big integers, returning the large value.
4859 // assumes both are normalized. if the return value is
4860 // negative, other is larger, if the return value is
4861 // positive, this is larger, otherwise they are equal.
4862 // the limbs are stored in little-endian order, so we
4863 // must compare the limbs in ever order.
4864 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 int compare(bigint const &other) const noexcept {
4865 if (vec.len() > other.vec.len()) {
4866 return 1;
4867 } else if (vec.len() < other.vec.len()) {
4868 return -1;
4869 } else {
4870 for (size_t index = vec.len(); index > 0; index--) {
4871 limb xi = vec[index - 1];
4872 limb yi = other.vec[index - 1];
4873 if (xi > yi) {
4874 return 1;
4875 } else if (xi < yi) {
4876 return -1;
4877 }
4878 }
4879 return 0;
4880 }
4881 }
4882
4883 // shift left each limb n bits, carrying over to the new limb
4884 // returns true if we were able to shift all the digits.
4885 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool shl_bits(size_t n) noexcept {
4886 // Internally, for each item, we shift left by n, and add the previous
4887 // right shifted limb-bits.
4888 // For example, we transform (for u8) shifted left 2, to:
4889 // b10100100 b01000010
4890 // b10 b10010001 b00001000
4891 FASTFLOAT_DEBUG_ASSERT(n != 0);
4892 FASTFLOAT_DEBUG_ASSERT(n < sizeof(limb) * 8);
4893
4894 size_t shl = n;
4895 size_t shr = limb_bits - shl;
4896 limb prev = 0;
4897 for (size_t index = 0; index < vec.len(); index++) {
4898 limb xi = vec[index];
4899 vec[index] = (xi << shl) | (prev >> shr);
4900 prev = xi;
4901 }
4902
4903 limb carry = prev >> shr;
4904 if (carry != 0) {
4905 return vec.try_push(carry);
4906 }
4907 return true;
4908 }
4909
4910 // move the limbs left by `n` limbs.
4911 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool shl_limbs(size_t n) noexcept {
4912 FASTFLOAT_DEBUG_ASSERT(n != 0);
4913 if (n + vec.len() > vec.capacity()) {
4914 return false;
4915 } else if (!vec.is_empty()) {
4916 // move limbs
4917 limb *dst = vec.data + n;
4918 limb const *src = vec.data;
4919 tinyobj_ff::copy_backward(src, src + vec.len(), dst + vec.len());
4920 // fill in empty limbs
4921 limb *first = vec.data;
4922 limb *last = first + n;
4923 tinyobj_ff::fill(first, last, 0);
4924 vec.set_len(n + vec.len());
4925 return true;
4926 } else {
4927 return true;
4928 }
4929 }
4930
4931 // move the limbs left by `n` bits.
4932 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool shl(size_t n) noexcept {
4933 size_t rem = n % limb_bits;
4934 size_t div = n / limb_bits;
4935 if (rem != 0) {
4936 FASTFLOAT_TRY(shl_bits(rem));
4937 }
4938 if (div != 0) {
4939 FASTFLOAT_TRY(shl_limbs(div));
4940 }
4941 return true;
4942 }
4943
4944 // get the number of leading zeros in the bigint.
4945 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 int ctlz() const noexcept {
4946 if (vec.is_empty()) {
4947 return 0;
4948 } else {
4949#ifdef FASTFLOAT_64BIT_LIMB
4950 return leading_zeroes(vec.rindex(0));
4951#else
4952 // no use defining a specialized leading_zeroes for a 32-bit type.
4953 uint64_t r0 = vec.rindex(0);
4954 return leading_zeroes(r0 << 32);
4955#endif
4956 }
4957 }
4958
4959 // get the number of bits in the bigint.
4960 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 int bit_length() const noexcept {
4961 int lz = ctlz();
4962 return int(limb_bits * vec.len()) - lz;
4963 }
4964
4965 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool mul(limb y) noexcept { return small_mul(vec, y); }
4966
4967 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool add(limb y) noexcept { return small_add(vec, y); }
4968
4969 // multiply as if by 2 raised to a power.
4970 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool pow2(uint32_t exp) noexcept { return shl(exp); }
4971
4972 // multiply as if by 5 raised to a power.
4973 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool pow5(uint32_t exp) noexcept {
4974 // multiply by a power of 5
4975 size_t large_length = sizeof(large_power_of_5) / sizeof(limb);
4976 limb_span large = limb_span(large_power_of_5, large_length);
4977 while (exp >= large_step) {
4978 FASTFLOAT_TRY(large_mul(vec, large));
4979 exp -= large_step;
4980 }
4981#ifdef FASTFLOAT_64BIT_LIMB
4982 uint32_t small_step = 27;
4983 limb max_native = 7450580596923828125UL;
4984#else
4985 uint32_t small_step = 13;
4986 limb max_native = 1220703125U;
4987#endif
4988 while (exp >= small_step) {
4989 FASTFLOAT_TRY(small_mul(vec, max_native));
4990 exp -= small_step;
4991 }
4992 if (exp != 0) {
4993 // Work around clang bug https://godbolt.org/z/zedh7rrhc
4994 // This is similar to https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/47746,
4995 // except the workaround described there don't work here
4996 FASTFLOAT_TRY(small_mul(
4997 vec, limb(((void)small_power_of_5[0], small_power_of_5[exp]))));
4998 }
4999
5000 return true;
5001 }
5002
5003 // multiply as if by 10 raised to a power.
5004 FASTFLOAT_CONSTEXPR20 bool pow10(uint32_t exp) noexcept {
5005 FASTFLOAT_TRY(pow5(exp));
5006 return pow2(exp);
5007 }
5008};
